title: The Sanakadi Guru Lineage
summary: The Sanakadi Guru Lineage — A source-conscious study of this subject.
body:
The traditional teacher-lineage of the Nimbarka Sampradaya begins with the four Kumaras—Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana and Sanatkumara. Devarshi Narada and then Shri Nimbarkacharya are remembered as the next principal links in this lineage. The tradition understands the transmission of knowledge not merely as the study of books, but as instruction and realisation passed from teacher to disciple.

## The Kumaras and Narada

The user-supplied research text quotes a passage from Shri Nimbarkacharya's Vedanta-Parijata-Saurabha on Brahma Sutra 1.3.8, referring to the instruction given by the revered Kumaras to their Guru, Shri Narada. The same research text cites the explanation of the sixth verse of the Dashashloki by Purushottamacharya, where 'Shri Naradaya' is explained as 'to our Guru'. These references help illuminate the lineage's own scriptural understanding.

## The testimony of Shri Srinivasa

The supplied research text also cites the invocation at the beginning of Shri Srinivasa's Vedanta-Kaustubha, which offers reverence to Hamsa, the Kumaras, Devarshi Narada and Nimbabhaskara. This is an important textual reference to the remembrance of the guru lineage. Its exact wording and edition details should be checked against the original book.

## Tradition and historical study

The traditional succession is a foundation of religious memory and sampradaya identity. The historical dating of each Acharya, their biographies and the precise relationships between them require separate evidence, such as manuscripts, inscriptions, institutional records and dated works. A traditional lineage and a modern historical chronology should therefore not be treated as the same kind of evidence.
